key_claims.claim: Antenatal magnesium sulfate administered in routine care is associated with a 17% relative risk reduction in death or cerebral palsy among very preterm neonates.
Approximately 45% of pregnancies with pregestational diabetes show angiogenic biomarker abnormalities indicative of occult placental dysfunction not captured by fetal size surveillance.
Quantitative stress-strain cervical elastography provides reproducible longitudinal stiffness measurements that distinguish term from preterm birth trajectories.
Partner-related and traumatic stressors independently associate with preterm birth and small-for-gestational-age outcomes, with race and ethnicity modifying some associations.
Risk of chronic hypertension in a subsequent pregnancy after severe-feature preeclampsia varies by gestational age at onset in the index pregnancy.
